conclusion.name: Sima Yu, Crown Prince Minhuai
conclusion.decision: all complete source members are same person
conclusion.uncertainty: No unresolved identity uncertainty in genuine named Chinese evidence. Typed wrong citations/foreign English occurrences and outside chronology are not endorsed and are not invented homonym evidence.

allIndividualMemberJudgments.rationale: Explicit Guangling Wang Yu established as crown prince under Hui, with He Shao/Wang Rong/Yang Ji tutors and capping. Same accession/tutor arrangement as target053s0201–0203.

primarySourceAnchors.zh: 秋八月壬午，立廣陵王遹爲皇太子，以中書監何劭爲太子太師，吏部尚書王戎爲太子太傅，衛將軍楊濟爲太子太保。
丙午，皇太子冠，丁未，見于太廟。

allIndividualMemberJudgments.rationale: Explicit 皇太子遹 deposed with three sons, mother Xie killed, murdered at Xuchang, restored and buried as 愍懷太子 at Xianping. Unique connected events establish the target; no inherited numeric year decides identity.

primarySourceAnchors.zh: 十二月壬戌，廢皇太子遹爲庶人，及其三子幽于金墉城，殺太子母謝氏。
癸未，賈后矯詔害庶人遹于許昌。
甲午，倫矯詔大赦，自爲相國、都督中外諸軍，如宣文輔魏故事，追復故皇太子位。
六月壬寅，葬愍懷太子于顯平陵。

allIndividualMemberJudgments.rationale: Explicit Minhuai confined at Xu and murdered during Hui/Jia disorder repeats target fate and place. Nephew in English, bogus office phrase and Ming-table date prose are extraction/editorial defects, not a second prince.

primarySourceAnchors.zh: 此歲正月，送湣懷太子，幽于許宮。
惠帝愚眊不寤，是月湣懷遂斃。

allIndividualMemberJudgments.rationale: Minhuai in Eastern Palace selecting eminent ministers’ sons, including Hua Heng, directly repeats target053s0205’s companion arrangement.

primarySourceAnchors.zh: 元康初，湣懷太子在東宮，選大臣子弟有名稱者以為賓友，略與華恆等並侍左右。

allIndividualMemberJudgments.rationale: Quoted memorial expressly recalls killed Minhuai and the resulting vacancy in imperial heirship before proposing Chengdu Ying. This same succession conflict identifies the prince; vacancy is not a claim of biological childlessness.

primarySourceAnchors.zh: 虓與東平王楙、鎮東將軍周馥等上言曰：自湣懷被害，皇儲不建，委重前相，輒失臣節。

allIndividualMemberJudgments.rationale: Target full identity: Yu/Xizu, Hui’s eldest son and Xie’s son, Minhuai, Guangling prince→crown prince, murdered by Sun Lü’s pestle at Xuchang, three sons. Narrator, forged prayer and retrospective letter frames stay distinguished.

primarySourceAnchors.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。
諡曰湣懷。
太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。

allIndividualMemberJudgments.rationale: Xi Jian/Wang Dun dialogue explicitly recalls Minhuai’s deposition as a prior moral test for Yue Guang/Man Fen; exact title and distinctive Hui court episode identify the target, without importing the later dialogue date.

primarySourceAnchors.zh: 及愍懷太子之廢，可謂柔而有正。
敦曰：「愍懷廢徙之際，交有危機之急，人何能以死守之乎！

allIndividualMemberJudgments.rationale: Actual 遹 in death edict and Yan Zuan’s defense, alongside crown-prince deposition and three sons, identifies Yu. Reject the foreign English Yu within Du Yu at0150 and He Yu at0194 as identity evidence; the clear Chinese core remains target Minhuai.

primarySourceAnchors.zh: 壬戌，帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛以太子書及青紙詔示之曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
今遹受罪之日，不敢失道，猶為輕於戾太子。

allIndividualMemberJudgments.rationale: Explicit former prince 遹 restored with Bin/Zang/Shang sons, posthumous Minhuai and Xianping burial directly identify the same target. Reject English Yu inside Xun Yu0290 and He Yu0285 as identity evidence, not genuine homonym uncertainty.

primarySourceAnchors.zh: 詔追復故太子遹位號，使尚書和郁帥東宮官屬迎太子喪於許昌，追封遹子虨為南陽王，封虨弟臧為臨淮王，尚為襄陽王。
太子遹之廢也，將立淮南王允為太弟，議者不合。
己卯，謚故太子曰愍懷；
六月，壬寅，葬於顯平陵。

allIndividualMemberJudgments.rationale: Tang Zhang Jiuling’s speech explicitly identifies 晉惠帝用賈後之譖廢愍懷太子 as a past warning. Named emperor/empress/title and exact deposition episode bridge the target without giving him Tang-era life dates.

primarySourceAnchors.zh: 晉惠帝用賈後之譖廢愍懷太子，中原塗炭。

sourceQuotes.zh: 太子患之，置針著錫常所坐氈中，刺之流血，錫，預之子也。
sourceQuotes.en: The heir apparent resented this, hid needles in the mat where Xi usually sat, and pricked him until he bled. Xi was the son of Du Yu.
sourceQuotes.literal: The Heir Apparent resented this, placed needles in the mat where Xi usually sat, and pricked him until he bled. Xi was the son of Du Yu.

typedOutsideQA.finding: Old p028 m0143 English Yu at code points130–132 is inside Du Yu, the father of Du Xi, and is not Crown Prince Sima Yu. c0055 includes s0150 as name evidence; that foreign English name must not be used as the prince’s identity name. Clear prince references0185/0201 remain. English already correctly names Du Yu; no editorial text proposal is needed.

sourceQuotes.zh: 於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
sourceQuotes.en: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Marquis of Chewu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
sourceQuotes.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Marquis of Chewu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

sourceQuotes.zh: 詔追復故太子遹位號，使尚書和郁帥東宮官屬迎太子喪於許昌，追封遹子虨為南陽王，封虨弟臧為臨淮王，尚為襄陽王。
sourceQuotes.en: An edict restored Yu's title, sent He Yu to bring the coffin from Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Xian as Prince of Nanyang and brothers Zang and Shang as princes.
sourceQuotes.literal: An edict restored the former Heir Apparent Yu's title and rank, sent the Masters of Writing He Yu leading Eastern Palace officials to meet the Heir Apparent's coffin at Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Yu's son Xian as Prince of Nanyang, and enfeoffed Xian's brothers Zang as Prince of Linhuai and Shang as Prince of Xiangyang.

These were separately addressed by actual31; this blind receipt preserves the old packet and requires an actual new-input delta check, without rebinding it. Genuine crown-prince references in both units remain contextually clear.
typedOutsideQA.identityConsequence: No alternative identity inferred. Retain source assertions unchanged for separate owned chapter QA; not fact/date approval.

sourceQuotes.zh: 天戒若曰，不宜緩恣奸人，將使太子冤死。
sourceQuotes.en: Heaven rebuked Jia Nanfeng's plot against the heir.
sourceQuotes.literal: Heaven warns: do not indulgently trust villains — it will make the heir die wronged.

typedOutsideQA.finding: c1982 treats 將使太子冤死 as an office held by Minhuai. It is an event prediction about unjust death, not an office designation.
typedOutsideQA.identityConsequence: No alternative identity inferred. Retain source assertions unchanged for separate owned chapter QA; not fact/date approval.

typedOutsideQA.finding: The English says Hui let his nephew be killed; target053 explicitly identifies Hui’s eldest son. c1985 marks a parent-of relation with kinshipTerm 子 as explicit although the cited source unit contains no 子 or explicit parentage phrase. sourceQuotes.zh: 晉惠帝用賈後之譖廢愍懷太子，中原塗炭。
sourceQuotes.en: Emperor Hui of Jin acted on Empress Jia's accusations and deposed Crown Prince Minhuai—and the heartland was laid waste.
sourceQuotes.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin took Empress Jia's slander and deposed the Crown Prince Minhuai; the Central Plain was scorched to ruin.

typedOutsideQA.finding: c1270 uses Tang Kaiyuan/Tianbao conversion boilerplate with an imported AD290–300 Jin career interval. Zhang Jiuling is recalling a past Jin prince; this is not new activity/date proof for Yu.
typedOutsideQA.identityConsequence: No alternative identity inferred. Retain source assertions unchanged for separate owned chapter QA; not fact/date approval.

sourceQuotes.zh: 虓與東平王楙、鎮東將軍周馥等上言曰：自湣懷被害，皇儲不建，委重前相，輒失臣節。
sourceQuotes.en: Xiao, together with King Mao of Dongping, General Who Guards the East Zhou Fu, and others, submitted words, saying: Since Minhuai was harmed, the imperial heir has not been established. Weighty responsibility was entrusted to the former minister, and he then lost the duty of a subject.
sourceQuotes.literal: Xiao, together with King Mao of Dongping, General Who Guards the East Zhou Fu, and others, submitted words, saying: Since Minhuai was harmed, the imperial heir has not been established. Weighty responsibility was entrusted to the former minister, and he then lost the duty of a subject.

typedOutsideQA.finding: c2283 says Minhuai was killed leaving no heir. 皇儲不建 describes an unfilled imperial succession position in the political memorial; it must not be promoted to a claim that Yu lacked biological children (target053 explicitly names three sons).
typedOutsideQA.identityConsequence: No alternative identity inferred. Retain source assertions unchanged for separate owned chapter QA; not fact/date approval.

sourceQuotes.zh: 十二月壬戌，廢皇太子遹爲庶人，及其三子幽于金墉城，殺太子母謝氏。
sourceQuotes.en: On the renxu day in the twelfth month Crown Prince Sima Yu was stripped of his title and imprisoned with his three sons in the Jinyong fortress, while his mother Lady Xie was put to death.
sourceQuotes.literal: In the twelfth month, on the renxu day, Crown Prince You was deposed to commoner status; together with his three sons he was confined in the Jinyong Fortress; the crown prince’s mother, the Lady Xie, was killed.

sourceQuotes.zh: 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝。
sourceQuotes.en: Twelfth month Jia feigned imperial illness to lure Yu to court.
sourceQuotes.literal: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.

sourceQuotes.zh: 及愍懷太子之廢，可謂柔而有正。
sourceQuotes.en: When they cashiered Crown Prince Minhuai he remained gentle yet principled.
sourceQuotes.literal: At the deposition of Crown Prince Minhuai he may be called yielding yet upright.

sourceQuotes.en: Wang Dun shot back, "During that crisis who could die on principle?
sourceQuotes.literal: Dun said: "At the deposition and exile of Minhuai, mutually there was crisis acute—how could men guard it with death!
